deep.reconstruction:
This page sits in a chapter on singular values ('s-numbers') ρ_i(u) of operators between Hilbert spaces. It covers three things.

(1) The end of the treatment of Schatten norms. A 'norme de Schatten' (modern term: symmetric gauge function, i.e. a symmetric absolute norm) N is first defined on R^(N), the finitely supported sequences. For an infinite sequence ξ=(ξ_i) of nonnegative numbers, set x_n=(ξ_1,…,ξ_n,0,…). Then N(x_n) increases with n, and one defines N(ξ)=lim_n N(x_n) ∈ [0,+∞]. With this definition, formula (27) of the previous page is a special case of the theorem (K.2). That formula reads N(|λ_1|,…,|λ_k|) ≤ N(ρ_1,…,ρ_k), i.e. Weyl's eigenvalue/singular-value inequality for symmetric gauge functions. Formula (28), the infinite-dimensional version, follows by passing to the limit. The next page confirms this reading.

(2) Theorem 3, 'second convexity theorem in Hilbert spaces'. Let E, F, G be Hilbert spaces, u: E→F and v: F→G linear (presumably compact or bounded). Let f be a continuous, symmetric, increasing function on the cone ρ_i ≥ 0 such that (t_i) ↦ f(e^{t_1},…,e^{t_n}) is convex on R^n. Then
f(ρ_1(vu),…,ρ_n(vu)) ≤ f(ρ_1(u)ρ_1(v),…,ρ_n(u)ρ_n(v)).
The proof applies the 'fundamental theorem' (Th. 1: a log-weak-majorization / Karamata-type theorem) to the two sequences (ρ_i(vu)) and (ρ_i(u)ρ_i(v)). The hypotheses needed are the partial-product inequalities ∏_{i≤k} ρ_i(vu) ≤ ∏_{i≤k} ρ_i(u)ρ_i(v). These are Horn's 1950 inequalities, obtainable from ρ_1 of exterior powers. The text says they are supplied by an earlier corollary (N°1, ...3, cor. 3).

(3) Corollary 1. Take a one-variable continuous (increasing) f with f(e^t) convex. Then Σ_{i≤n} f(ρ_i(vu)) ≤ Σ_{i≤n} f(ρ_i(u)ρ_i(v)) for every n, and hence also for the infinite sum (31).

A (partly crossed-out) commentary follows. It says the sequence (ρ_i(vu)) attached to vu admits all the majorations that would hold if one had ρ_i(vu)=ρ_i(u)ρ_i(v). This is a heuristic of 'multiplication' of singular-value sequences. A remark about corollary 5 of Th. 1 is left to the reader.

The next page specialises to f(t)=t^s and gets the Hölder inequality for Schatten classes: ||vu||_s ≤ ||u||_p ||v||_q with 1/s = 1/p + 1/q. It also gets |Tr u| ≤ Σ s_i(u).

Purpose: a self-contained majorization-based theory of Schatten–von Neumann ideals and their norm inequalities. This is background for Grothendieck's tensor-product and nuclear-operator work; compare his Bourbaki exposé on convexity inequalities in von Neumann algebras with trace.
errors: On this page the composite is written ρ_i(uv) although u: E→F and v: F→G, so only vu is defined. The next page corrects this to vu.

Corollary 1 as transcribed omits 'croissante' (increasing). Monotonicity of f is needed, since only weak (sub-)majorization of log-singular values is available. The hypothesis is presumably in the illegible part.
The limit definition N(ξ)=lim N(x_n) can give +∞. Statement (28)/(31) in infinite dimensions should be read in [0,+∞]. This is a minor point the page does not make explicit.

ideas.what: Extension of a symmetric gauge function from finitely supported sequences to arbitrary nonnegative sequences by monotone limit
ideas.modern_name: symmetric norming function / symmetric gauge function on c_00 extended to sequence spaces (Gohberg–Krein)

ideas.what: f(ρ(vu)) ≤ f(ρ(u)ρ(v)) for symmetric increasing f with f∘exp convex, via log-majorization
ideas.modern_name: Horn's inequality for singular values of products plus the multiplicative (log-)majorization theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: A. Horn (1950), H. Weyl (1949), Pólya; Gel'fand–Naimark; Marshall–Olkin exposition
ideas.where_published: Possibly related material in Grothendieck, 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace', Sém. Bourbaki 1955 (exposé 113); unsure whether this exact statement appears

ideas.what: Σ f(ρ_i(vu)) ≤ Σ f(ρ_i(u)ρ_i(v)), leading to Schatten Hölder ||vu||_s ≤ ||u||_p||v||_q
ideas.modern_name: Hölder inequality for Schatten–von Neumann classes

ideas.what: Heuristic that singular-value sequences of a composite satisfy all majorations as if ρ_i(vu)=ρ_i(u)ρ_i(v)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, independent rederivation of Weyl–Horn majorization and the Schatten-class Hölder inequality, all known by 1950–51. It is careful expository work with no result or connection absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The references read '(25' and '(26' in the first paragraph are very likely '(27)' and '(28)'. The intended text is 'La formule (27) est un cas particulier du théorème, … La formule (28) en résulte par passage à la limite', as confirmed by the next page.
ρ_i(uv) should be read as ρ_i(vu) given the stated domains; the next page uses vu.
Corollary 1 hypothesis likely reads 'f(t) une fonction continue croissante de t ≥ 0'.
'il suffit d'appliquer le th. 1 … aux deux suites (ρ_i(uv))_{i≤n} et (ρ_i(u)ρ_i(v))_{i≤n}'; the inserted words are 'de l'appl. b' / 'n° 29) du th. 1'.
